item.title: Excessive and persistent dog fouling., 18th August
item.description:
Good morning, This is a second report of the same issue, but at a different location. It concerns the Brosse Way side of the large care home, Crown Meadow Court. This side of the care home is experiencing the same severe levels of dog fouling as the other side. Dog excrement is left every six feet or so, and there are flies everywhere — particularly unpleasant in this heat. This is not a problem that will simply go away; the same dog keeps returning and fouling the area. From a health and safety perspective, why should the residents and staff of this care home have to put up with the smell and the flies because of one or two selfish dog owners? A regular offender is a man of Mediterranean or Persian appearance (occasionally a woman) with a German Shepherd or Belgian Malinois. He walks up from the Trinity Village area to the spot I have marked on the map, allows the dog to foul without clearing it, then returns the way he came. I am a dog owner myself but do not feel able to challenge him. I raised this previously and appreciate the signs that were put up, but they have not stopped the behaviour. Thank you for looking into this.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Brosse Way, Bromley Common, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
